paraphrase: Another rite, which removes all defects in their (observances), is taught — one the gods obtained from Hara by austerity to strengthen their own rites: in the month of Śrāvaṇa, at its end, or in Nabhasya, having offered the pavitra (thread-garland) to Śambhu, one should complete the year's ritual.

paraphrase: Knowing their own office to be very hard to fulfil, teachers and others who seek mastery should strive for self-possession; that self-possession, which is the yogin's state, belongs to one who has conquered the senses, and conquest of the senses comes gradually through practising breath-control and the rest. Breath-control (prāṇāyāma), withdrawal (pratyāhāra), fixation (dhāraṇā), meditation (dhyāna), examination (vīkṣaṇa), recitation (japa) and absorption (samādhi) are the limbs; the possessor of the limbs, yoga itself, is the eighth.

paraphrase: Prāṇa is the air described before; its restraint is its exertion, marked by propelling, drawing in and holding, and it removes the faults of ritual. When the mind then tastes a little happiness, withdrawal is to be practised — turning back from everything. Thereby turned away from contact of senses and objects, the mind becomes fit for fixation on a place chosen at will. Thought upon that object, directed again and again, is meditation; when it becomes one continuous flow, that is called absorption. Recitation is the uttering of it, bringing the object of meditation face to face; examination (ūha) is the scrutiny arising after the object has been conceived — knowing the place, what is to be rejected and accepted there, what sustains it and what opposes it.
